outputs.L1: The mass term of the transformed quark fields gives rise to effective contact interactions of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) type. We discuss the parameters of the model that maps a system of noninteracting transformed fields onto quarks interacting through NJL contact terms.
outputs.L2: The mass contribution of the redefined quark fields generates effective local interactions of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) form. We also examine the model parameters that establish the correspondence between free transformed fields and quarks coupled through NJL-type contact interactions.
outputs.L3:
The mass term associated with the transformed quark fields gives rise to effective local interactions when rewritten in terms of the original quark variables. These induced interactions have the structure of Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) contact terms, typically involving local four-quark operators in the relevant scalar, pseudoscalar, and other symmetry-allowed channels.

Consequently, the model establishes a mapping between two complementary descriptions: a system of transformed fields that is non-interacting, or effectively free, and a system of physical quarks that interacts through NJL-type contact forces. In the quark representation, the effects of the field transformation are therefore encoded in the coupling constants and operator structure of the resulting NJL interaction terms.

The parameters controlling this correspondence include the mass scale appearing in the transformed-field description, the strength and form of the field transformation, and any ultraviolet cutoff or regularization scale required to define the contact theory. Together, these quantities determine the effective NJL couplings and thus govern the magnitude and phenomenological consequences of the induced quark interactions.
outputs.L4:
The study develops a formal connection between a theory of transformed quark fields and an effective Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. Starting from the mass term written in terms of the transformed fields, the analysis rewrites the theory using the original quark variables. Because the field transformation is generally nonlinear or mixes different quark components, a mass term that is quadratic in the transformed fields generates higher-order terms in the original fields. In particular, the resulting four-fermion operators have the structure of local NJL contact interactions.

The parameters entering the field transformation determine the strength and form of these induced interactions. By comparing the transformed mass term with the standard NJL Lagrangian, the study identifies how the effective four-quark coupling is related to the transformation parameters and to the relevant quark-mass scales. It also considers the conditions required for the mapping to remain physically meaningful, including the consistency of dimensions, signs, symmetry properties, and limiting behavior. When the transformation is removed or its nonlinear contribution vanishes, the effective interaction disappears and the usual free-field description is recovered.

A central result is that a system that is noninteracting when expressed in terms of the transformed fields can appear as an interacting system when described using the original quark variables. The apparent quark interactions are therefore induced by the change of field representation rather than introduced as independent fundamental forces. At the effective level, these interactions take the form of NJL-type contact terms, which are widely used to model low-energy quark dynamics and phenomena associated with dynamical symmetry breaking.

This correspondence provides a useful interpretation of NJL models. It shows that their local four-fermion interactions may, under suitable assumptions, be understood as the effective consequence of a transformed-field mass term. The mapping also offers a systematic way to relate phenomenological NJL couplings to parameters characterizing the underlying field transformation. Although such a contact description does not reproduce the full momentum-dependent dynamics of quantum chromodynamics, it can serve as a compact and tractable framework for studying nonperturbative quark behavior at low energies.

Overall, the work demonstrates that free transformed fields and interacting quark fields can represent equivalent descriptions of the same system within the domain in which the mapping applies. By clarifying how the NJL interaction emerges and which parameters control it, the study strengthens the theoretical basis for using contact-interaction models as effective descriptions of quark interactions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize how a quark-field transformation can generate effective Nambu–Jona-Lasinio contact interactions from a mass term.
counterfactuals.output:
A field-dependent redefinition of the quark variable can turn a quadratic mass term into an expression containing four-quark operators. Schematically, define

\[
q=\chi+\frac{G}{m}\Big[c_s(\bar\chi\chi)
+c_p\,i\gamma_5\tau^a(\bar\chi i\gamma_5\tau^a\chi)\Big]\chi+\cdots ,
\]

with a corresponding transformation for \(\bar q\). Substituting this into

\[
-m\bar q q
\]

and expanding to first order in \(G\) gives

\[
-m\bar\chi\chi
+G\left[(\bar\chi\chi)^2
+(\bar\chi i\gamma_5\tau^a\chi)^2\right]+\cdots ,
\]

after choosing the coefficients and signs appropriately. The generated quartic terms are the scalar–pseudoscalar contact interactions characteristic of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model. More general color, flavor, or Dirac structures can be produced by changing the bilinears in the transformation.

The kinetic term simultaneously generates derivative interactions and higher-order multi-quark operators, while the path-integral measure may contribute a Jacobian. Thus an exact invertible field redefinition does not introduce new physical dynamics—it only redistributes interactions among operators. An “effective NJL interaction” emerges when the transformed theory is expanded and truncated at the leading local four-fermion level.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: What follows from the mass term of the transformed quark fields, and which model parameters characterize the mapping to interacting quarks?
counterfactuals.output:
After the chiral field transformation \(q=U^{\gamma _5/2}Q\), the quark mass term becomes

\[
-M\bar Q\,U^{\gamma _5}Q .
\]

Expanding \(U^{\gamma _5}\) generates interactions of the transformed quarks with the Goldstone fields—first a pseudoscalar quark–pion Yukawa term, followed by multi-pion contact terms:

\[
-M\bar QQ-\mathrm{i}\frac{M}{f_\pi}\bar Q\gamma _5\tau^a\pi^a Q+\cdots .
\]

Thus the quark–pion coupling obeys the constituent-level Goldberger–Treiman relation \(g_{\pi qq}=M/f_\pi\). The mapping to interacting (constituent) quarks is characterized mainly by the constituent mass \(M\), the chiral scale \(f_\pi\) or equivalently \(g_{\pi qq}\), and, in regulated versions of the model, a cutoff \(\Lambda\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a brief abstract-style statement explaining how non-interacting transformed fields can be mapped onto quarks with NJL-type interactions.
counterfactuals.output: A nonlinear field redefinition can map non-interacting transformed fermionic fields onto quark variables whose effective action contains local four-fermion couplings. The transformation’s field dependence—and, in the path integral, its Jacobian—repackages the free dynamics into scalar, pseudoscalar, and related quark bilinears characteristic of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model. Equivalently, auxiliary bosonic fields may be introduced and integrated out to generate the NJL interaction, providing an effective description of dynamical chiral symmetry breaking.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the emergence of effective four-quark contact terms after a field transformation and mention the role of the model parameters.
counterfactuals.output:
After redefining the fields—often by shifting or eliminating a heavy bosonic/mediator field—the transformed Lagrangian contains terms quadratic in quark bilinears. These appear as local four-quark interactions, for example
\[
\mathcal L_{\rm eff}^{(4q)}
=G_S\!\left[(\bar q q)^2+(\bar q i\gamma_5\vec\tau q)^2\right]
-G_V(\bar q\gamma_\mu q)^2+\cdots .
\]
They represent short-range mediator exchange and can drive dynamical chiral-symmetry breaking, condensate formation, and mesonic bound states.

Their strengths are fixed by the original model parameters. Typically, integrating out a mediator of mass \(M\) and coupling \(g\) gives \(G\sim g^2/M^2\), while mixing angles, bare masses, and regulator or cutoff scales determine the relative scalar, pseudoscalar, vector, and other channels. An exact invertible field transformation does not change physical observables; it only reorganizes the interactions, although truncated approximations may retain an apparent dependence on the transformation parameters.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Give a concise two-sentence overview of a model that converts free transformed quark fields into quarks interacting through NJL contact terms.
counterfactuals.output: The Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model describes quarks with local four-fermion contact interactions, often expressed through a Bogoliubov transformation from free quasiparticle fields to interacting constituent-quark fields. These interactions dynamically break chiral symmetry, generate constituent quark masses and mesonic bound states, but do not provide confinement.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
